tags: why do dogs tuck their tail
script: A dog's tail says a lot more than just happy or sad. When it's tucked tightly between their legs, they're covering their scent glands near the base of the tail, an instinctive move that signals fear or submission to whoever's nearby. It's the canine version of making yourself smaller when you feel unsafe. A low, slowly wagging tail usually means they're unsure or cautious, while a stiff, high tail can actually signal alertness or even a warning, not friendliness. Only a loose, wide wag paired with relaxed body language really means happy. Learning to read tail position tells you exactly what your dog is feeling. Want to go deeper?
